hook_text: Pour ALL of Earth's water into one 10-litre bucket. The part you can actually drink? A few teaspoons.
clip_script: Imagine every drop of water on Earth poured into one ten-litre bucket. Oceans, ice caps, rivers, clouds, the water underground, the water inside every living thing — all of it, one bucket. About nine and a half litres is sea water — salty, undrinkable. Skim off the fresh water and most of that is ice, locked in the polar sheets. What remains — the fresh, liquid, gettable water that every city, farm, animal and plant on land must share — is in the order of a few teaspoons. That is the hydrosphere: a planet drenched in water, and a civilisation living off the teaspoons.
visual_style: A giant bucket filling with blue; salt water tinted and locked away, ice frosted over, then a zoom to a trembling teaspoon that the whole animated world queues up to share.
pacing: Grand pour, quick locking-away of salt and ice, dramatic slow zoom onto the teaspoons.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson — one drop's journey through oceans, rocks, plants and you.
